body: Yes it does, but it appears this is because I am using the Muffin/footprint plugin, which creates a newEntity.  This was resulting in things being converted i.e. my dateTime were coming back in the SOURCE timezone instead of the expected UTC timezone.  Upon further investigation, the "BUG" maybe with the footprint plugin.
Does simply downgrading cakephp core resolve your issue?
Well then the issue does seem to be related to core rather than Footprint plugin.

The diff I posted earlier was intended to be a minor optimization to avoid loading `Cake\I18n\DateTime` and its parent classes until absolutely necessary. I think it might be simplest if we revert 2d153f080c16483c8a44346b5ddfce1673263c5e

Before reverting, it would be helpful to figure out _why_ that change broke your custom type, as I don't see any uses of `_datetimeInstance` in the linked code. Does the Footprint plugin also use custom datetime types?

`Footprint` doesn't use custom datetime types. Footprint maintains logged in user's record as entity by creating one from Auth's user array. That's the only place where marshaling of date could be involved.

But on Slack @birdy247 claimed that he has this problem even when reading a record for other models. So personally I have no idea what could be the source of issue.
@ADmad Interesting, I'm happy to revert the optimization if @birdy247 is confident it solves the issue he's having.
@birdy247 could you share an isolated issue repo (github link) or prep a Unit Test?

@birdy247 Yes we have understood the problem in general. The point is we need to narrow down the exact cause of the issue. Try the [patch](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/9066#issuecomment-230050226) @markstory provided and let us know if it fixes your problem.
